title: Etale cohomology of a finite coproduct of geometric points
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $C=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the finite coproduct of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. For an abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], choose the geometric point $\bar c_i$ on the $i$-th summand, with geometric stalk $F_{\bar c_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Then the etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] satisfies $H^q(C,F)=0$ for every $q>0$, and the canonical map $H^0(C,F)\to\prod_{i\in I}F_{\bar c_i}$ is an isomorphism (the product is finite).

proof.text: Compare H^q(RΓ(F[0])) with the classical right derived functor of Γ using homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso. The terminal-object isomorphism ΓNatIsoSheafSections induces an isomorphism on right derived functors, and Sheaf.subsingleton_H_iff_isZero_rightDerived identifies their vanishing with subsingleton Sheaf.H F q. These comparison declarations are already proved in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafCohomologyRightDerived and WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.PlusCompatibility.

source.place: Section 03QQ and Lemma 03QU: cohomology as the derived functor of global sections; existing proved Lean comparison lemmas

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology] with the identity geometric point to each sheaf (c_i)^*F. In positive degree its cohomology is zero, so its Ext cohomology is subsingleton by Step 1. The bijective map of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly] embeds Sheaf.H F q into the product of these subsingleton groups. Hence Sheaf.H F q is subsingleton, and Step 1 proves the required derived vanishing. The given c_i form the coproduct cofan because hc identifies them with Sigma.ι.

proof.text: For the specified degree-zero map, let U_i be the open image of c_i. The open immersion gives an isomorphism Spec k ≅ U_i. The standard coproduct homeomorphism proves that the U_i cover, and sigmaι_eq_iff proves their pairwise disjointness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-disjoint-etale-sections-product] to identify F(C) with the product of F(U_i), including the empty case.

source.place: Tag 03P9, sheaf condition for the disjoint coproduct cover

proof.text: The algebraically closed field k is strictly henselian: it is henselian, and its residue field is separably closed. Each U_i is therefore a strictly henselian local open, with the specified point c_i factoring through its isomorphism from Spec k. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-strictly-henselian-open-germ] directly to F on C. Each F(U_i) → F_(c_i) is the canonical germ and is invertible. The relation Point.toPresheafFiber_w identifies restriction from F(C) followed by this germ with the global germ at c_i. Taking the product gives precisely the Pi.lift in the theorem, not an unspecified isomorphism. Restriction Γ(F) → F(C) is invertible since C is terminal in its small étale site; both preceding derived-to-underived degree-zero comparison maps are already isomorphisms. Compose these isomorphisms to finish.
